name: Generating and transforming graphs
gist: Papers on creating new graphs or modifying existing ones using generative models and optimization techniques to solve graph-based problems.
explain: Most graph learning papers predict things about existing graphs. But sometimes you want to generate new graphs—design new molecules, create synthetic social networks for simulation, find better graph structures by optimization—because you need new examples or solutions. This requires a different kind of model: one that can produce structured data, respecting the constraints (molecules have valid bonds, social networks have realistic patterns), since random graphs won't work.

The hard part is the combinatorial explosion. A molecule's atoms can bond in countless ways, most of which are chemically impossible. A graph with N nodes can have up to N squared possible edges. You can't enumerate all possibilities. Also, the order in which you generate things matters: if you add an atom first, then try to add a bond to it, you might back yourself into a corner. You need a way to generate step-by-step while respecting global constraints.

Papers use generative models: diffusion (start with noise, gradually refine it into a valid graph), flow matching (learn to transform from one distribution to another), and autoregressive approaches (predict one thing at a time, conditioning on what you've already generated). They tackle combinatorial optimization: given a graph, find a better version by modifying it, using learned models or optimization algorithms. They use graph augmentation—adding or removing edges—as a way to generate training data for other tasks. Some incorporate chemical knowledge (atoms have valence limits) or social knowledge (realistic networks follow patterns like preferential attachment) to guide generation toward realistic outputs.

papers.title: CheckMate! Watermarking Graph Diffusion Models in Polynomial Time
papers.contribution: CheckMate provides polynomial-time verification with strong robustness against graph modifications like isomorphism, while maintaining generation quality.

papers.title: From Moments to Models: Graphon-Mixture Learning for Mixup and Contrastive Learning
papers.contribution: Develops GMAM for graph mixup augmentation and MGCL for contrastive learning, achieving new SOTA on six of seven supervised datasets and competitive performance on unsupervised benchmarks.

papers.title: NetDiff: Graph Diffusion with Improved Global Capabilities to Generate and Update Mobile Network Topologies
papers.contribution: Reaches over 95% of target performance with constant inference time, outperforms heuristic and omnidirectional baselines on graph-level metrics.

papers.title: Out-of-Distribution Graph Models Merging
papers.contribution: The framework is architecture-agnostic and operates without source/target domain data, with theoretical analysis and experiments demonstrating effectiveness.

papers.title: GLAD: Bidirectional Structure-Attribute Alignment via Latent Graph Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: GLAD significantly outperforms GAN-based baselines in attribute recovery quality and downstream task performance, with tighter variational lower bounds on joint log-likelihood.

papers.title: RADE: Random Add-Drop Edge as a Regularizer
papers.contribution: Provably aligns training and inference; mitigates both overfitting and over-squashing; hyperparameter-free in practice with strong node and graph classification results.

papers.title: ReLaSH: Reconstructing Joint Latent Spaces for Efficient Generation of Synthetic Hypergraphs with Hyperlink Attributes
papers.contribution: ReLaSH explicitly accounts for hypergraph structure and jointly models hyperlinks with attributes, enabling realistic synthetic hypergraph generation.

papers.title: SuperHype: Hypergraph Generation via Graph-Superposition Decomposition
papers.contribution: Reproduces local and global connectivity patterns with superior fidelity compared to state-of-the-art hypergraph generation baselines across five datasets.

papers.title: Towards Generative Graph Matching for Graph Edit Distance Computation
papers.contribution: Generates diverse edit paths with accuracy comparable to exact solutions while running faster than existing hybrid approaches.
